title: Why Buying a Business Beats Starting One: 15 Real Reasons
description:
Most people start a business from zero. The smart money often buys one that already works. Here are 15 real reasons buying can beat starting, a full example deal with SBA financing, and the risks nobody talks about.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:37 How we got the numbers
2:05 Reason 1. Cash flow from day one
3:07 Reason 2. Proven survival
4:01 Reason 3. Banks lend on history
5:01 Reason 4. Seller financing
5:57 Reason 5. Trained employees
6:50 Reason 6. Existing customers
7:45 Reason 7. Systems and suppliers
8:53 Reason 8. Brand and reputation
9:44 Reason 9. Real data to decide with
10:35 Reason 10. Baby boomer retirements
11:32 Reason 11. Lower total cost of risk
12:38 Reason 12. Room to improve
13:37 Reason 13. Training from the seller
14:25 Reason 14. Faster path to scale
15:15 Reason 15. Ownership without inventing
16:06 The risks nobody talks about
17:00 When starting from scratch is the better choice
18:04 Three buyers, three stories
19:36 Where to find businesses for sale
20:34 Ten questions to ask before you buy
21:31 Five mistakes first time buyers make
22:10 How small businesses are priced
23:32 Your first 100 days as an owner
24:26 Angle 1: The numbers
26:11 The other end: selling someday
27:19 Angle 2: The psychology
29:10 Angle 3: The playbook
30:58 Questions people ask
32:32 Recap
33:40 What to do next

Sources:
- Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics (survival rates of new establishments: about 1 in 5 fail in year one, about half by year five)
- U.S. Small Business Administration, 7(a) loan program (business acquisitions, equity injection, personal guarantees)
- Example deal: simplified illustration ($120,000 owner earnings, 3x multiple, 10% down, 10-year loan at an illustrative 10.5% rate)

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video16.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
